hook.text: The Sydney Opera House was estimated at four years. It took sixteen. Every human makes this same mistake daily.

buildup.text: Kahneman and Tversky named it the planning fallacy. People consistently underestimate how long tasks will take.

discovery.text: The bias comes from imagining best-case scenarios. You picture the work flowing perfectly with zero interruptions.

twist.text: Even knowing about this bias does not fix it. Awareness helps, but your gut still whispers 'this time is different.'

climax.text: Use reference class forecasting: check how long similar tasks took before and use that as your real estimate.

punchline.text: Check last time. Estimate from history, not hope.

quiz.question: What causes the planning fallacy?
options: People are naturally pessimistic about timelines
People imagine best-case scenarios and ignore past experience
